name: Elementary
title: Everyday Life in German
tagline: Talk about your past, make appointments and handle daily situations.
overview: A2 turns survival German into everyday German. You will add the dative, the perfect tense and modal verbs, then use them in real situations: renting a flat, visiting a doctor, travelling and talking about what happened last week. Explanations stay in English while the German you produce grows longer and more independent.
levelGoal: By the end of A2 you can describe your past, make and change appointments, explain simple problems, and hold a short conversation about work, travel and health.
canDo: Talk about past events using the Perfekt and Präteritum.
Make, reschedule and cancel appointments politely.
Describe symptoms to a doctor and understand simple advice.
Compare things and express preferences while travelling.

modules.title: Talking About the Past
modules.summary: Tell people what happened using the perfect tense and the most common past forms.

lessons.title: The Perfekt with haben & sein
lessons.titleDe: Das Perfekt mit haben und sein
lessons.summary: The everyday past tense: build participles and choose the right auxiliary.
objectives: Form regular and irregular past participles.
Choose between haben and sein correctly.
Tell a short story about yesterday.

keyPhrase.de: Wir haben gestern einen Film gesehen.

lessons.title: Präteritum of Common Verbs
lessons.summary: war, hatte, konnte and musste — the compact past forms you will hear and read constantly.
objectives: Conjugate war and hatte in all persons.
Use konnte and musste in past narratives.
Recognise Präteritum forms in short texts.

keyPhrase.de: Als Kind war ich oft in den Bergen.
keyPhrase.en: As a child I was often in the mountains.

lessons.title: Telling Past Experiences
lessons.summary: Connect events with time expressions and sequencing words to tell a clear story.
objectives: Use time expressions such as letztes Jahr and danach.
Sequence events with zuerst, dann and schließlich.
Write a short travel anecdote in the past.

keyPhrase.de: Letztes Jahr bin ich nach Hamburg gereist.
keyPhrase.en: Last year I travelled to Hamburg.

modules.title: Cases in Depth
modules.summary: Master the dative, tell direct and indirect objects apart, and use two-way prepositions.

lessons.title: The Dative Case
lessons.summary: Give, help and thank the right person with the dative case and its pronouns.
objectives: Form the definite and indefinite articles in the dative.
Use dative pronouns mir, dir, ihm and ihr.
Apply dative verbs such as helfen, danken and gefallen.

lessons.title: Accusative vs Dative
lessons.summary: Two objects in one sentence: decide who receives what.
objectives: Identify direct and indirect objects in a sentence.
Order dative and accusative objects naturally.
Use the right case after common verbs and prepositions.

keyPhrase.de: Ich gebe dem Kind einen Apfel.
keyPhrase.en: I give the child an apple.

lessons.title: Two-Way Prepositions
lessons.summary: Location or movement? Use the dative for where and the accusative for where to.
objectives: Identify the nine two-way prepositions.
Choose dative for position and accusative for direction.
Describe where objects are and where people go.

keyPhrase.de: Die Katze springt auf den Tisch.
keyPhrase.en: The cat jumps onto the table.

modules.title: Verbs & Clauses
modules.summary: Modal verbs, separable verbs, reflexives and your first subordinate clauses.

lessons.title: Modal Verbs
lessons.summary: Say what you can, must, may, want and should do — with the verb at the end.
objectives: Conjugate können, müssen, dürfen, wollen, sollen and mögen.
Use the modal sentence bracket correctly.
Make polite requests with könnten and würden.

keyPhrase.en: I have to work longer today.

lessons.title: Separable & Reflexive Verbs
lessons.summary: Split verbs at the right moment and talk about yourself with reflexive pronouns.
objectives: Separate prefixes in main clauses and keep them in subordinate clauses.
Use reflexive pronouns in the accusative and dative.
Distinguish true reflexive verbs from ordinary verbs.

keyPhrase.de: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
keyPhrase.en: I am looking forward to the weekend.

lessons.title: Subordinate Clauses
lessons.titleDe: Nebensätze mit weil, dass, wenn, obwohl
lessons.summary: Give reasons, state facts, describe conditions and concede with verb-final clauses.
objectives: Place the conjugated verb at the end of a subordinate clause.
Choose between weil and dass.
Use wenn for conditions and obwohl for contrast.

keyPhrase.de: Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland studieren möchte.
keyPhrase.en: I am learning German because I want to study in Germany.

modules.title: Life in Germany
modules.summary: Compare, describe, make appointments and handle travel, health and housing.

lessons.title: Comparatives & Superlatives
lessons.summary: Say something is bigger, better or the best — and compare options with als.
objectives: Form comparatives with -er and superlatives with am -sten.
Use common irregular forms such as besser and am besten.
Compare two things with als.

keyPhrase.de: Der Zug ist schneller als der Bus.
keyPhrase.en: The train is faster than the bus.

lessons.title: Adjective Declension Basics
lessons.summary: Put adjectives in front of nouns and give them the right ending.
objectives: Decline adjectives after definite articles in all three cases.
Recognise the ending patterns in the plural.
Describe people and objects with adjective + noun phrases.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe den neuen Film gesehen.

lessons.title: Appointments, Doctor & Travel
lessons.summary: Make appointments, explain symptoms and talk about future plans.
objectives: Make, move and cancel an appointment politely.
Describe symptoms and understand basic medical advice.
Talk about future plans using the present tense and werden.

keyPhrase.en: I would like to make an appointment.
